findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is visible to anyone with instance metadata access or API describe-instance-attribute permissions, and often ends up in logs/version control.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data at rest unencrypted and readable if the underlying storage or snapshots are exposed.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, so any copies or shares of this snapshot expose data in cleartext.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional network boundary (e.g., load balancer/WAF), directly exposing the web application to the entire internet over unencrypted HTTP.
Egress rule allows all traffic (-1 protocol, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no network-level containment if the instance is compromised, facilitating data exfiltration.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances in this subnet, increasing the internet-facing attack surface, especially combined with the security group allowing SSH/HTTP from anywhere.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, expanding the attack surface for any workloads placed there.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure or tampering of sensitive network flow data.
